Tiles come through your traffic proxy when it holds an Esri key (best). Otherwise paste an Esri API key (only without a proxy), restricted to the app's site since it's visible in the page. Source: World Imagery (imagery only) or Imagery with labels. Opacity slider. Check key tests both sources. Through the proxy, tiles you view are kept on the device (up to 6,000) and show again offline.

Not in the Options window but in its own section (the NOTAMs tab on the full-screen map): Traffic proxy: the proxy address (empty = traffic off). NAIPS areas, Brief in NAIPS ↗, NAIPS area page ↗. Download with your NAIPS login: not available yet (awaiting Airservices authorisation). NAIPS briefing: Paste from clipboard, Load briefing, Open PDF / file, Clear briefing. Speak traffic alerts (on): also covers "Wires ahead". See Weather and NOTAMs and Traffic.
Aircraft type, callsign, aeroplane / helicopter, runway and Tower/CTAF choice are set in Radio calls (see Radio calls).
Plan check, under the flight plan's leg list, opens the Pre-flight brief: everything along your plan at a planned altitude, speed and departure time, in one list you can copy or print.

All are kept on the phone. Tap Check to run it again after a change. Box Use Altitude ft Planned altitude for legs without their own altitude (leg overrides from Edit are used where set). GS kt (TAS kt with a wind) Your speed. With a wind chosen it's taken as TAS and each leg gets its own groundspeed. Wind none; entered: one wind for the route (from °T, kt) read off the grid point wind chart; nearest TAF: each leg takes the surface wind forecast by the closest aerodrome TAF in your briefing at the time you'd be there. Departure (local) Your departure time. ETAs, tower hours, NOTAM times, SIGMETs and day/night use it. Burn L/h, Fuel L Fuel flow and fuel on board, for the time and fuel table. Reserve min Your own final reserve. Empty = the CASA figure. OAT Outside air temperature for hover performance where no TAF or METAR gives one. A TAF wind is the wind on the ground, not at your altitude; the NAIPS text briefing has no winds aloft. An entered wind from the grid point wind chart is the better figure.

NAIPS briefing: when it was issued, warned when over 6 hours old, ending before you arrive, or missing one of the plan's aerodromes. Weather at each plan aerodrome at its ETA: TAF category, wind and weather then, with any TEMPO/INTER/PROB; the METAR; the ATIS. Area QNH, and the number of SIGMETs/AIRMETs on the route at your level.

In order, with distance and ETA: waypoints (a coast leg's turn points are left out); the CTAF or tower of the nearest aerodrome as it changes: tower hours at your ETA, the split-tower side, the call name ("Barwon Heads traffic"); broadcast areas; area or ATC frequency changes at your altitude (class, limits, "clearance required"); zones list their ATIS frequency; the squawk at a tower where you land; restricted, prohibited and danger areas you'd enter at that altitude, with activity and status at ETA; NOTAM temporary zones, and NOTAM obstacles within 1 NM of track; SIGMETs/AIRMETs at your planned level at ETA; last light, if the plan ends after it.
With a wind chosen: each leg's heading (°M), groundspeed and time. A coast leg is one row: "track along the coast", "HDG varies", average groundspeed.
With Burn L/h (and optionally Fuel L): time and fuel per leg, fuel remaining at the end of each leg, and totals. Rows below the reserve are red. Leg times use the wind when one is chosen.

The CASA final reserve (Part 91 MOS 19.02), VFR: Day Night Helicopter 20 min 30 min Aeroplane 30 min 45 min The category is the Aeroplane / Helicopter choice in Radio calls. It's night when the departure or the arrival is outside first to last light, using the Departure time. The fuel line says which applies, e.g. "reserve 20 min (helicopter, VFR day, CASA Part 91 MOS 19.02) = 33 L". Enter Reserve min to use your own figure. The line then says "your setting" and notes when it's below the CASA minimum. Clear the box to go back. This is the fixed final reserve only. Add any variable or contingency fuel your operator requires.

For each leg: the highest terrain or NOTAM obstacle within 2 NM of track, +1,000 ft, rounded up. If terrain isn't loaded for part of a leg it says "terrain partly loaded" and retries while the window is open. This is a guide from 30″ terrain data, not a published LSALT.
Aerodrome NOTAMs are listed under the leg arriving there (departure under leg 1); area NOTAMs under the first leg that passes within 1 NM; the rest under "Other".
With a W&B profile set up, a row gives the take-off, landing and zero-fuel result against the envelope (see Weight and balance).

When your W&B profile has hover ceiling tables (see Hover performance inputs), the brief has a Hover performance table for the departure and every point you land at: Column From ETA The plan's time there. Temperature The TAF at ETA, else the METAR, else the OAT you enter in Plan check. QNH TAF, METAR or area QNH; else 1013 hPa assumed, and the table says so. Pressure altitude Aerodrome elevation + (1013 − QNH) × 30 ft. Density altitude Pressure altitude + 120 ft per °C above ISA. Weight Your W&B take-off weight less the fuel burnt to that point. IGE / OGE max The maximum weights from your hover ceiling tables at that density altitude. Margin How far under the limit you are. Amber when the margin is under 5%. Red when you're over the limit, or the density altitude is outside your table. Density altitude here is an approximation. The flight manual's hover charts govern. The app has no performance figures of its own: the table only uses the numbers you copied from your flight manual.

Every power line the route crosses (Geoscience Australia transmission lines, 66 kV and up) and every NOTAM obstacle within 0.5 NM of it, in order along the route: Power lines: how high you'll be above the ground where you cross it, at the leg's planned altitude. The lines' heights aren't in the data, so it can't give a clearance over the wires themselves. Amber under 500 ft above the ground. Obstacles: height AMSL, how far off track, and your clearance at the planned altitude. Amber under 500 ft, red when the obstacle is above you. The same marks are on the plan's elevation profile and the map's side view.

The current SUPs and AICs for the plan's aerodromes, and ones placed within 10 NM of the route (wind farms, restricted areas, reporting points), with their dates. Below them, folded, the general ones with no place (e.g. amendments to the DAH or ERSA GEN). Titles only: read each on the Airservices website. See Aerodrome card.

At the end, the brief checks this device has: the app and AIP data; terrain along the route (3 NM either side); chart tiles for each ticked sheet the route crosses; a NAIPS briefing under 6 hours old and valid to arrival. It names chart sheets on the route you haven't ticked, with a Tick them button. Coast legs: "turn points stored with the plan".
Copy text copies the whole brief as plain text. Print / PDF opens it for printing or saving as a PDF.

The radio call guide fills in the calls for the aerodrome on the card, from your position, level and callsign. Reminders bring the right call up at the right time. Check the wording against AIP ENR 1.1 and local procedures.

Open Radio calls and enter your aircraft type and callsign, and choose aeroplane or helicopter. All are saved on the device. Type the callsign as the registration (ABC or VH-ABC) and it's spelled phonetically: "ALPHA BRAVO CHARLIE". VH- is dropped, 9 is NINER. Anything with spaces (POLAIR 31) or one word of 5+ letters (RESCUE) is left as typed. Category (aeroplane / helicopter) also sets minimum heights for altitude suggestions, the CASA fuel reserve and highlighting of helicopter procedures. Runway picker: the aerodrome's runways (RH marked). The calls use the runway you pick.

The standard calls from AIP ENR 1.1: inbound, overflying, joining, straight-in, taxiing, lining up and departing. Distance, compass point and level are filled in from your position. Within 1.5 NM of a VFR waypoint the position starts with it ("over Carrum, 5 miles south").

When the tower is open (from ERSA's tower hours, allowing for daylight saving): listen to the ATIS and note the letter; taxi call to Ground, ready call; Transponder · before entering the CTR (the squawk code); inbound call naming the ERSA reporting points (e.g. CARR, BAW, BTO, ACE, SHOL or GMH at Moorabbin) at the CTR entry altitude ("over Carrum" once within 3 NM of a reporting point); the downwind report where ERSA requires it. Type comes before callsign: "Moorabbin Tower, Bell 206 ALPHA BRAVO CHARLIE, …". Outside tower hours it switches to CTAF calls. You can force Tower or CTAF. The ATIS letter you've noted goes into the calls ("received Charlie").

Tap ✎ on any call to change how it's worded, e.g. at Moorabbin "…, inbound for the southern approach." The call is a template: {station}, {type}, {callsign}, {position}, {level}, {atis}, {runway} and {place} take the values of the moment. Tap a token to insert it. Words in [brackets] show as yours to fill. A preview shows the call as it would be said now. Save it for this aerodrome or every aerodrome (per procedure: tower or CTAF). An aerodrome's own wording wins over the every-aerodrome one. Your wording is marked YOURS (YOURS · ALL) and also used for the 10 NM inbound reminder. Back to the standard call removes it.
Crossing 10 NM towards an aerodrome (closing, more than 3 NM out), a row appears once per approach with the call filled in.

Lilydale traffic, Bell 206 ALPHA BRAVO CHARLIE, 10 miles south, 1,500 feet, inbound, estimate circuit at time 36, [joining intentions], Lilydale "time 36" is the UTC minutes of your ETA. With the aerodrome in your plan, the ETA follows the plan (a coast route and reporting points included, wind-corrected where a wind is known). With only a Go to, it's the straight line at your groundspeed. For a tower open at your ETA it's the tower call on the frequency the tower tile would use (reporting-point rules included), with the ATIS placeholder, and a SQUAWK badge. The Go to tile flashes. Distance and level keep updating. It goes when you tap it, inside 4 NM, or after 4 minutes. It re-arms beyond 12 NM.

Ballarat traffic, Cessna 175, ALPHA BRAVO CHARLIE, 10 miles north, 4,500 feet, transiting east to west, Ballarat For non-towered aerodromes (or a tower that's closed) within reach that you're not landing at. Direction from your track. None while you're in controlled airspace, none for strips inside an open tower's zone, and none within 15 NM of where you're landing. It goes once you're back outside 10.5 NM or after 4 minutes.

No plan: your Go to aerodrome, or one of its ERSA reporting points (a Go to CARR counts as landing at Moorabbin). A town or other point near an aerodrome doesn't. With a plan: points marked Land (the last point by default; change it in Edit), plus the aerodrome of a direct-to (a diversion) until you resume.

After you've dismissed it (or it went by itself), tap the → CTAF tile (your Go to or plan aerodrome) or the CTAF tile within 15 NM. The call comes back, worked out for where you are now: inbound where you land, transit for a field you pass (none for a towered field with its tower open you're only passing). It stays until you tap it, are 15 NM away, or 4 minutes pass. With tile enlarging on, the first tap enlarges the tile and the second brings the call back.

When class A, C or D airspace (or a control zone) is within 10 NM ahead at your level, the first call in the list is a clearance request: Avalon Approach, Bell 206 ALPHA BRAVO CHARLIE, 2 miles east of Torquay, 1,500 feet, received [ATIS YMAV], request clearance to transit [direction / via …] at 1,500 feet A zone transit goes to the approach unit ERSA lists (by sector where there are several). With no approach unit in ERSA it goes to the tower (your side of a split tower). When you're landing at the zone's aerodrome there's no clearance request: the tower inbound call is the request. Within 5 NM a CLEARANCE CALL row appears in the top bar with the same request. Tap it to dismiss for that airspace; it goes once you're inside or after 4 minutes. The clearance request is a trial. Some zones, such as Moorabbin, are entered with an inbound report at a reporting point rather than a clearance request. The ATIS letter and route are yours to fill.

Inside a control zone you're transiting (not landing at its aerodrome), Radio calls shows the zone's calls on the unit you entered with: In the zone (position report when ATC asks) and Clear of the zone, instead of the CTAF calls of strips under it. The CTAF and ATC tiles show the approach unit ("APP 133.55 Avalon App · zone transit"). Within 3 NM of the field the tower shows when you're departing or in the circuit; a transit that came in from outside stays with approach.

When you're landing at a towered aerodrome, the inbound row shows the code to set before entering the zone: a code you typed in the clearance notes wins; else a VFR code from ERSA, e.g. SQUAWK 0100 for Essendon; else the AIP ENR 1.6 class C/D code 3000 (Moorabbin's ERSA gives no VFR code). The same code is on the tower Radio calls card and the tower row of Plan check. Flying past without landing shows no code. Leaving the zone, the calls remind you of 1200 for VFR in class G/E.

Open ATIS and clearance from the ATIS / clearance button at the top of Radio calls, the NEXT CLASS row, the CLEARANCE row, or the ATIS frequency in the controlled aerodrome row. ATIS letter: pick the letter you heard (A–Z) for that aerodrome. It goes into the tower, taxi, clearance-request and inbound calls and shows after the ATIS frequency ("ATIS 120.9 (C)") for 60 minutes. Listen to ATIS: tune the ATIS, tap it, and the app transcribes the broadcast into fields you can Use. See ATIS capture. Squawk, Level and Route / instructions: shown on a CLEARANCE 4123 · A015 · via CARR · ATIS C row while you're in or about to enter controlled airspace. The notes clear 2 minutes after you leave controlled airspace, or 45 minutes after you wrote them if you never went in. Clear all clears them now; Done closes. With transcription on, a Use button on a heard transmission can fill the letter, QNH, squawk, level and route for you (only when you tap it).

In the same window (also More → Read-back pad): a lined pad to write a clearance with your finger, like a kneeboard. Undo takes back the last stroke, Wipe pad clears it. A second finger or your palm is ignored. A picture of what you wrote shows on the CLEARANCE row so it stays in sight while you read back. It clears with the notes. With transcription on, the app can also compare your spoken read-back with the clearance (see Read-back check).

The red SOS button on the map opens Emergency: MAYDAY / PAN PAN, and choose the Emergency (engine failure, smoke in the cabin, low fuel, medical, uncertain of position, weather …), Intentions (forced landing, landing immediately, diverting to the nearest aerodrome, returning) and People on board. The call in order: MAYDAY ×3, station, type and callsign, nature, intentions, position (from the nearest aerodrome or VFR waypoint, e.g. "5 miles north-east of Leopold"), level, heading, POB. Who to call and on what frequency for where you are: the ATC unit for your band, the tower in a zone, else the CTAF. Squawk 7700, ELT/PLB, and 121.5 if no answer (or relay through another aircraft). Your lat/long, GPS altitude, track, groundspeed and UTC. Nearest places to land: aerodromes and helipads with °M, NM and TWR/CTAF. Tap one to set it as Go to. From GPS and the app's data: check before you rely on it.

pt: Top bar tiles and alert rows
t: The top bar is what you glance at in flight. Tiles are always there; alert rows only appear when there is something to tell you. On the phone's full-screen map the main tiles float over the map; tap one for the whole bar.

pt: Top bar tiles and alert rows
t: Tile What it shows GPS An icon only. Green: accuracy better than 50 m; orange to 300 m; red worse, no fix or no permission; grey before the first fix. Orange with SIM in the simulator. If no new fix arrives for 5 s it turns orange with the age under it ("7s"), red from 15 s. Hold or hover for the accuracy. TRK / HDG GPS track in °M, or the compass heading (HDG) when you're too slow for a track. W/V from the GPS wind estimate after you've turned through 120° or more in 3 minutes. Hidden while heading tape A or D is on (the tape shows your track). GS Groundspeed in kt, with last light under it ("last 0920Z" or "night"), and the head or tail wind along your track when the wind is known ("HW 12", "TW 7 · 258/20"). PLAN Magnetic bearing to the active waypoint (or Go to), its name, and the turn from your track (L/R; orange at 10° or more). No wind correction. The label says PLAN, DIRECT (direct-to, plan paused) or GO TO (no plan). ALT GPS altitude in ft above mean sea level, with height above the terrain (AGL) under it. CLASS The airspace class at your position and altitude, e.g. G, or G·D when you're also in a danger area, with its name under it (D373). CAP / LL "CAP A085": the top of the band you're in (where the next class starts), and "LL SFC": its lower limit. GPS altitude is geometric, not pressure altitude. On Android the app turns the GPS height into height above mean sea level with an EGM96 geoid grid (+2 m at Barwon Heads, +62 m at Cairns, −32 m at Perth). iPhones already report sea-level altitude. Near a step boundary go by your altimeter. AGL is from the terrain grid and errs low.

pt: Top bar tiles and alert rows
Top bar tiles and alert rows
t: The CTAF of the aerodrome closest to you, with its code and, on a line of its own, the name to use on the radio and where you are from the field: Riddell traffic · 4.0 NM NW, or "overhead" within 0.5 NM. It follows the map's CTAF areas: with Split overlapping CTAF areas on, the tile changes at the halfway line between two aerodromes on different frequencies. Elsewhere it keeps the aerodrome you're in while within 10 NM of it. During tower hours it shows TWR. A split tower shows your side: at Moorabbin TWR W 123.0 west of the field, TWR E 118.1 east. ERSA reporting-point rules win over the bearing: near Carrum it reads TWR W 123.0 · via CARR (RWY 17/35). Without a side it says "see ATIS". On the ground at a towered aerodrome (under 30 kt, within 200 ft of its elevation) it shows GND. Passing a towered aerodrome that isn't in your plan or Go to, or transiting its zone more than 3 NM from the field, it shows the approach unit, e.g. APP 133.55 Avalon App. No aerodrome within 10 NM: the broadcast area frequency if you're in one ("127.1 · Abrolhos broadcast area"), else the area frequency for your altitude (AREA 123.35 Melbourne Ctr, "no aerodrome within 10 NM (YAPO 51 NM)"). The AREA tile then hides so the frequency isn't shown twice. CARD YMMB ✕ badge: the Aerodrome card shows another aerodrome (you tapped it). Tap ✕ to go back to the closest. CARD without ✕: the flight plan chose it. "YMMB · 2 NOTAM" when the aerodrome has active NOTAMs from your briefing. Tap it (a second tap if tiles enlarge) within 15 NM to bring back the inbound or transit call (see Radio calls).

pt: Top bar tiles and alert rows
t: The class G/E area frequency at your position and altitude, or ATC (coloured by class) in controlled airspace, with the unit ("Melbourne Ctr", "Moorabbin Twr"). Where more than one area frequency is stacked over you, the unit line adds where yours starts ("Melbourne Ctr · LL SFC"). In a control zone you're transiting it shows the approach unit ("APP 133.55 Avalon App · zone transit").

pt: Top bar tiles and alert rows
t: Under each: the frequency you can expect next and how far away, e.g. "next 121.6 in 9.0 NM · YMEL" or "next ATC 132.0 in 4.0 NM · Melbourne App". The path ahead is the rest of your plan, or your track (out to 80 NM) at your current altitude. Nothing is shown when you're stationary.

pt: Top bar tiles and alert rows
t: Dashed and marked →, while a Go to or plan is set: → CTAF / → TWR: the aerodrome at the Go to point or the nearest within 10 NM of it, with distance and time to go. Tower hours are checked at your ETA ("TWR closed at ETA"); a split tower gives the side you're approaching from. → AREA / → ATC: the area or ATC frequency over the Go to point at your current altitude. Badges show PLAN 2/14, DIRECT or GO TO. When → TWR and → ATC are the same frequency, only → TWR shows. They hide within 0.3 NM of the point or when they'd repeat the top tiles. On the phone's map they're compact (frequency, aerodrome or unit, badge).

pt: Top bar tiles and alert rows
t: When the closest aerodrome has a tower or approach in ERSA: ATIS (or AWIS), TWR (E/W at a split tower), GND, DEL, APP and the first DEP. At Moorabbin: ATIS 120.9 · TWR 118.1 E · TWR 123.0 W · GND 134.25. Outside tower hours it says "TWR closed" and strikes through TWR, GND and DEL. A second row does the same for your Go to aerodrome. Tap the ATIS frequency to open ATIS and clearance.

pt: Top bar tiles and alert rows
t: HDG: compass heading in °M (with the learnt alignment), and drift when moving. →HDG: heading to steer to the next waypoint or Go to, corrected for the wind (the GPS wind estimate under 20 minutes old, else Plan check's wind). Shows "WCA R6°" or "no wind". Second line: heading and distance to the destination. TOT: time over the next waypoint in UTC at your groundspeed (Plan check's speed below 20 kt), with the time to go, and the destination's time along the rest of the plan. On a coast leg the next point is the leg's end, not the turn point. Hold for local times. With heading tape A (the default) or D on, the tape replaces HDG and →HDG, so the row is just TOT. Tape A sits at the very top. See Heading display for styles A, C and D.

pt: Top bar tiles and alert rows
t: Row When it shows NEXT CLASS (red) Class A, C or D (including control zones) or a restricted area starts within 10 NM ahead at your altitude: class or area, limits, distance, unit and frequency (your side of a split tower), ATIS where the zone has one, "clearance". Ignores G/E changes, danger areas, and an R area that will be off when you get there. Tap for ATIS and clearance. IN You're inside a restricted, prohibited or danger area at its levels: name, limits, status (RA1/2/3), activity, hours, and the NOTAM status from your briefing. Also NOTAM temporary zones and SIGMETs/AIRMETs you're in. One line per area; an area that is off is greyed. AHEAD (in the IN row) A SIGMET/AIRMET on your plan (at each leg's altitude) or track within 60 NM / 40 min: "AHEAD SIGMET … in 36 NM · 18 min". LSALT While moving or with a plan: highest terrain or NOTAM obstacle within 2 NM of your next 10 NM plus 1,000 ft, rounded up to 100 ft, and where it is. Amber when that point is within 500 ft below you, red at or above. A guide from 30″ terrain, not the published IFR LSALT. WIRES (red) Your track crosses a transmission line within 2 NM while you're under 500 ft above terrain at 20 kt or more. Local distribution lines aren't in the data. TRAFFIC The nearest warning target (within 2.5 NM and ±600 ft): clock position, distance, height, registration and type. Red. INBOUND CALL / TRANSIT CALL Crossing 10 NM towards an aerodrome: the call filled in. With SQUAWK 3000 (etc.) where you land at a towered field. See Radio calls. CLEARANCE CALL Controlled airspace within 5 NM ahead at your level: frequency and the clearance request. Tap to dismiss. CLEARANCE Your clearance notes (squawk, level, route, ATIS letter, read-back pad picture) while in or about to enter controlled airspace. FUEL The fuel timer: fuel left, time and distance to your reserve. Amber under 30 min to reserve, red at it. SARTIME Countdown to your SARTIME or flight note. Amber in the last 30 min or once landed, red once passed. CHECKLIST A checklist offered for the phase of flight. Tap to open. RADIO The last two transcribed transmissions (within 2 min), with Use suggestions and the read-back check. Orange for 30 s when your callsign is heard. LAST LIGHT From 30 min before last light: "LAST LIGHT in 20 min 0920Z (8:20 pm)", amber then red from 10 min; after it, "NIGHT … first light …".

pt: Top bar tiles and alert rows
s: Tap a tile to enlarge it
t: On a small screen, tap a tile and it grows in place and stays big until you tap somewhere else. Tap it again while it's big for what it normally does (the whole top bar, the fuel timer, your clearance notes). In landscape the enlarged tile pops in front of the map. Turn it off in Options → Top bar tiles → Tap a tile to enlarge it (on by default); then one tap acts straight away.

pt: Top bar tiles and alert rows
t: When the CTAF or AREA tile changes frequency (or CTAF → TWR, AREA → ATC) it pulses amber, 5 times by default. Options → Top bar tiles → Flash CTAF and AREA when they change sets the number; 0 turns it off.

pt: Top bar tiles and alert rows
t: Options → Top bar tiles lists every tile and alert row with a small example. Each has two ticks: one for the phone (and a tablet held upright), one for the tablet in landscape. The column in use now is highlighted. The tablet's ticks start as a copy of the phone's. All are on by default; the others widen to fill the row. Alert rows only appear when there's something to show. Think twice before hiding NEXT CLASS, IN, TRAFFIC or LAST LIGHT.

The Traffic button on the map shows ADS-B traffic from the internet, with TCAS-style symbols and spoken alerts. Not TCAS. Internet ADS-B only shows aircraft transmitting ADS-B that a ground receiver hears, typically 5–10 s late, and coverage is patchy at low level. It doesn't replace looking out or the radio.

Positions from adsb.lol (adsb.fi as a fallback), fetched through a small proxy (a Cloudflare Worker) every 10 seconds while there's signal and the app is in front. The proxy address is Traffic proxy in NOTAMs (NAIPS) and traffic. Empty turns traffic off. The proxy shares its data between everyone using it: it asks the feed for 100 NM round the middle of a 0.5° area (about 30 NM across) at most every 8 seconds, and each phone gets the aircraft within its own Traffic distance (up to 100 NM). If the feed doesn't answer, it keeps using the last positions for up to a minute; an aircraft whose position is more than a minute old is left out. If the feed says it's busy, the app waits as asked and the status line says when it will try again.

Symbol Meaning Grey hollow diamond Other traffic. Cyan filled diamond Within 6 NM and ±1,200 ft. Large red dot, white edge, red ring Warning: within 2.5 NM and ±600 ft. Drawn on top of everything. The number is the height difference in hundreds of feet (+03 = 300 ft above), with ↑ or ↓ when climbing or descending more than 500 ft/min. Every airborne target has a stick along its track; cyan and warning targets also have a line to where they'll be in 1 minute. Heights are GNSS altitude converted to mean sea level, to compare with your GPS altitude; pressure altitude when there's no GNSS altitude. The corner of the map shows "ADS-B 3 · 2 s". After 30 s without an update it says "stale", the symbols fade and there are no alerts.

Tap a target for a dashed ring and a box with registration and callsign, type, altitude (and the difference from yours), track °M and groundspeed, and distance, bearing and clock position from you. It updates live. Tap it again or anywhere else to clear.

For the nearest warning target, a red TRAFFIC row: "11 o'clock 1.7 NM · 300 ft above · VH-VOZ C172". Spoken: "Traffic, 11 o'clock, 2 miles, 300 feet above", once a minute per aircraft. Turn it off with Speak traffic alerts (NOTAMs (NAIPS) and traffic). Only with data under 30 seconds old.

Traffic distance (Options → ADS-B traffic): 10, 15, 25, 40, 60 or 100 NM around you (default 25). Further shows more but uses more data. The status line says if the proxy limited it. Traffic symbol size (Options → ADS-B traffic): Small to Largest. The tap area grows with it. Speak traffic alerts also covers the spoken power line warning.

Your aircraft never raises an alert or shows as a target. It's recognised by: registration or flight id matching the callsign in Radio calls (ABC → VH-ABC); its ICAO address once learnt; moving with you: within 0.6 NM, track within 25°, groundspeed within 20 kt, height within 600 ft; or simply within 0.15 NM and 300 ft. A target matching (3) on two updates in a row is learnt as yours for that callsign. The status line shows "Own aircraft ignored: 7C… VH-ABC". Set your callsign so another aircraft you fly isn't mixed up. A close formation partner on the same track and speed would also be treated as you.

With Traffic on, every update is saved with the flight log while you're flying (20 kt or more in the last 5 minutes; not on the ground, in the simulator, or your own aircraft). Each flight's GPX then has one track per aircraft, named by registration or flight and type, with its altitude, speed, track, distance from you, warning level and closest approach. Kept 90 days like the rest of the log.

The app can listen to the radio through your headset or the audio panel and write each transmission down, flag calls with your callsign, offer the ATIS and clearance details for your notes, capture an ATIS and check your read-back. Everything is in Options → Radio audio and transcription. Transcription and suggestions are an aid only. The speech model mishears callsigns and numbers. Your ears and your read-back come first. Nothing is filled in without your tap: check it against what you heard.

First check what audio the tablet can actually hear. Connect the headset (a Bluetooth headset such as the Bose A30), or a cable from the audio panel through a USB-C audio adapter. Tap List inputs (allow the microphone once) and pick the input. Bluetooth and USB inputs are named as such. Tap Listen and watch the meter while you talk on the intercom, then while the radio plays an ATIS or a CTAF call. A Bluetooth headset may send the tablet only its own boom microphone (in "call" mode), not the radio and intercom audio: the meter and a 30 s recording show what actually arrives. If the radio isn't there, use a cable from the audio panel's recording or music output into a USB-C audio adapter. Meter moves for the radio: radio audio reaches the tablet. Moves only when you talk: the headset sends just your microphone. Use the audio panel cable instead. Raw audio (ticked by default) turns off the phone's echo cancelling, noise suppression and automatic gain, which can cut radio audio as "noise". Record 30 s, Play back and Save recording let you hear what the tablet got. A Bluetooth headset sends call-quality audio while the tablet listens to it. Nothing leaves the device (except with the online speech service, below).

Whisper (on the tablet, slower) Browser speech recognition (fast) Where it runs On the tablet. Works offline once the model is downloaded. The browser's own recogniser. Offline and on-device only where the browser has an offline speech pack. Speed A few seconds per call (on a desktop about a third of the call's length; a tablet is slower). If it falls behind it skips the oldest waiting call and says so. Text as the call is spoken. Setup Pick a model and Download model once with signal: Standard model (41 MB) or Better model (77 MB, about 2x slower). It stays stored across updates; Delete model removes it. Install offline pack appears when one can be downloaded. Privacy Nothing leaves the device. Without an offline pack it uses Google's online speech service: the audio goes to Google and it needs signal. The Engine note says so. The browser engine listens to the input picked in the audio test (Chrome; an older browser uses the default microphone and says so). Both engines are told local names so they come out right: aerodromes within 30 NM (with Tower/Ground/Approach where ERSA has them), VFR points within 20 NM, the current area unit, and your type and callsign. Without that, "Moorabbin Tower … Carrum" came out "Murabintaur … Karam". The log, alerts, Use suggestions, ATIS capture, read-back check, flight-log transcripts and hands-free checklists work with either engine.

Tick Transcribe the input. Each transmission (picked out from the background hiss) becomes a line with its time, newest first. Sensitivity (Low / Normal / High) sets how much louder than the hiss a sound must be to count. Higher catches quieter calls but also more noise. Your callsign is highlighted; frequencies, squawk codes, QNH, heights, runways and the ATIS letter are bold. Spoken numbers ("three four zero one", "one thousand five hundred") are read as digits. The last two lines (within 2 minutes) show on a RADIO row in the top bar, which stays while Options is closed. Tap it for the whole log. Turn the row off under Top bar tiles. It keeps listening when Options is closed, until you untick it. Transcribe the recording does the same for the 30 s recording. Copy puts the log on the clipboard; Clear empties it.

When a transmission has your callsign (the last three letters, spoken phonetically or as letters, from Radio calls), the tablet vibrates twice, plays a two-note chime (through the headset when that's the sound output) and marks the RADIO row orange for 30 s. Turn it off with Alert when my callsign is heard.

A Use button appears on the log line and the RADIO row when a transmission has: an ATIS letter ("information Charlie") and/or QNH; and, with your callsign: a squawk code, a level ("not above 1,500", "climb to 3,000", "maintain…", "flight level 95") and a "cleared …" route. Tap Use to put them in the ATIS and clearance notes. The ATIS goes to the aerodrome named in the transmission, else the one nearby. Nothing is filled in without the tap.

In the ATIS and clearance window there's a Listen to ATIS button. It needs the input set up as above. Tune the ATIS on the radio. Tap Listen to ATIS. The app listens through the chosen engine for up to 2 minutes, or until the broadcast repeats. Stop ends early. It shows what it heard as fields: Information (letter), Runway, Wind, Visibility, Cloud, Temperature, QNH, Other. Tap Use to save the letter, QNH and the fields as the ATIS for that aerodrome. The saved ATIS shows in the dialog and in the aerodrome card's Weather section as ATIS heard hhmmZ, and the letter goes into your calls. The ATIS text doesn't go into the radio log. An aid only: check each field against what you hear.

With transcription on and Check my read-back ticked (on by default): When a clearance or instruction to your callsign is heard with a squawk, level, heading, QNH, runway or frequency, the next transmission within 30 s that has your callsign or those items is treated as your read-back and compared. The log line and RADIO row show Read-back ✓, or what differs or is missing, e.g.: Read-back: not above 1500 (cleared 1000) · missed squawk 3401 A mismatch gives a short vibration. It can only compare what both transmissions were heard as, and it can't tell who is speaking. A ✓ doesn't mean your read-back was right; a mismatch may be the model mishearing. Your own ears decide.

Each transcribed line is kept with its time and position (not in the simulator). Each flight's GPX (Flight log button, Options → Flight logs, Google Drive) has them as waypoints named "Radio 0412Z" with the words as the description. Replay shows them on the RADIO row at their time.

The transcription section shows how much memory the speech model takes: about 290 MB for the standard model once it has run, on top of the app. It's freed when the app is closed or the model deleted. Options → Render timing has a memory line too (the app's own memory, the speech model, roughly the device's RAM, and how much is stored).
A checklist can read itself out and listen for your responses through the same input. See Checklists.

NOTAMs and weather come only from a NAIPS briefing you load into the app. There is no live NOTAM feed. The app reads the briefing and puts each item where it matters: the aerodrome card, the map, the top bar and the pre-flight brief. Get a fresh NAIPS briefing before each flight. The app only knows what was in the last briefing you loaded, and says when it has expired.

The settings are in NOTAMs (NAIPS) and traffic (the NOTAMs tab on the full-screen map). Set your NAIPS areas (e.g. 9300, up to five, comma separated). Tap Brief in NAIPS ↗. It opens an area briefing (NOTAMs, 12 h) in your browser, signed in as you. NAIPS area page ↗ just opens the form. Tick weather in NAIPS if you want METARs, TAFs, SIGMETs and area QNH. Bring the result back, any of these ways: copy it and paste into NAIPS briefing (or Paste from clipboard), then Load briefing; on Android, share the text or a saved PDF to the installed app; Open PDF / file: a briefing saved with the browser's Save as PDF / Print, or a .txt. The app only opens NAIPS; it never reads it. The briefing is kept on the phone for offline use. Clear briefing removes it. The section header shows how many NOTAMs are active, or that the briefing has expired. Download with your NAIPS login appears in the same section but is not available yet. NAIPS's terms prohibit automated access without Airservices' written authorisation, which has been requested. Until then, use Brief in NAIPS and bring the briefing back as above.

Each NOTAM's location, number, replaces, FROM/TO, EST, PERM, schedules (HJ, HN, DAILY 1800-0700) and active periods. Limits (SFC TO 400FT AGL, 4000FT AMSL TO FL210) and positions (WI 3NM RADIUS OF ARP, PSN of obstacles). Restricted and danger area NOTAMs (R352 PARTIAL ACT, R360D ACT) tied to the area. The "no current NOTAM" list at the end ("none current" on those aerodromes' cards). METARs/SPECIs, TAFs, ATIS, area QNH and SIGMETs/AIRMETs from the weather part.

CTAF and Go to tiles: "YMMB · 2 NOTAM". Aerodrome card: a NOTAMs box, open by itself for CLSD / U/S / NOT AVBL, key words highlighted, UTC with local time in brackets. Map: dashed red circles for airspace and warning NOTAMs; temporary zones as red dashed polygons; obstacles as tower symbols (red within 300 ft of your altitude or above). Press and hold: NOTAMs covering that point, NOTAMs naming a restricted or danger area there, and obstacles within 1 NM. Flight plan and pre-flight brief: NOTAMs within 1 NM of a leg and for its aerodromes, grouped by leg. IN row: NOTAM temporary zones and circles with limits that you're inside.

From the loaded briefing each R, D and M area gets a status: ACTIVE when a NOTAM activates it ("R352 PARTIAL ACT", "R360CEF ACT" = R360C, E and F), with the NOTAM's limits and end time. When the briefing lists it under "no current NOTAM", it's active if ERSA says H24, or by its ERSA daily hours or HJ/HN. OFF when a NOTAM deactivates it ("D342 DEACTIVATED"), or it's under "no current NOTAM" and ERSA says it's activated only by NOTAM. A NOTAM's own schedule is applied, with sunrise and sunset worked out for the area. With no briefing, or once it has expired, there's no status and the app says "check status". Active areas are stronger on the map with "ACT →1300Z"; areas that are off are grey dashed, "OFF". The IN row leads with "ACTIVE NOTAM C4/26 →1300Z". NEXT CLASS ignores an R area that will be off when you get there; the CLASS tile ignores areas that are off.

Current SIGMET/AIRMET areas are drawn on the map in amber long dashes, labelled with the phenomenon and levels. The same area in two FIRs is shown once. Press and hold inside one to see it, with its raw text. IN row when you're inside one at its levels. AHEAD: one on the rest of your plan (at each leg's altitude) or straight ahead within 60 NM / 40 min: "AHEAD SIGMET … in 36 NM · 18 min". Optionally spoken (Options → Spoken alerts). Cancelled ones are dropped.
From the briefing's "AREA … QNH" blocks: shown in each aerodrome's Weather section (even without a METAR there) and on the briefing status line.

The aerodrome card's Weather box decodes the METAR: wind, QNH, temperature and dew point, density altitude, and crosswind and headwind per runway (magnetic wind, best runway first). An ATIS from the briefing shows first, with changed fields highlighted and an old ATIS flagged. An ATIS you captured from the radio shows as "ATIS heard hhmmZ" (see ATIS capture).

The TAF is shown as an hour-by-hour table (scroll sideways; the current hour highlighted; local times): Flight category badge: VFR, MVFR, IFR or LIFR from ceiling and visibility (US-style; a guide only). Weather icon and words, visibility, ceiling, cloud layers, wind (arrow pointing downwind, °T), speed and gusts. The RMK temperatures and QNH (3-hourly, interpolated between). A TEMPO / INTER row with the temporary conditions and their category when worse. FM replaces the forecast from its time; BECMG changes what it lists from the start of its period. Turbulence remarks, TAF3 and amendments are shown as notes; CNL and NIL get a one-line message. The raw TAF is under Original.

The Wx layer (on by default) rings each aerodrome with a METAR or TAF in its flight category: green VFR, blue MVFR, red IFR, purple LIFR. It uses the METAR for now (when under 90 minutes old), else the TAF. For aerodromes still ahead on your plan, the TAF at your ETA there. A dashed outer ring means a TEMPO, INTER or PROB period is worse. Tap the aerodrome for its card and the decoded weather.

The Radar layer lays the latest RainViewer radar image over the map (Australian radars, 10-minute steps, about 1 km detail), with its time and age at the bottom left, red once over 30 minutes old. Online only; refreshed every 5 minutes. RainViewer's free service is for personal and educational use.
